projects.name: Assessing Deep Generative Models on Time Series Network Data
projects.subtitle: Synthetic Data, Time-series, and GANs (remember those?)
projects.description:
Wireless networks need AI to manage themselves automatically, but AI requires large amounts of training data that simply isn't publicly available. We investigated whether synthetic data generated by AI models could substitute for real network traffic data. We tested two GAN-based models and one auto-regressive model, comparing how well they could generate realistic synthetic time-series network data — especially when only a small amount of real data was available for training.

We found that GANs consistently outperformed the auto-regressive approach and that forecasting models trained on GAN-generated data achieved error rates comparable to those trained on real data. Supplementing small amounts of real data with synthetic data also led to modest but measurable performance improvements. To reference one number, a downstream prediction model trained purely on DoppelGANger generated data resulted in a MAPE only 3% less than the same model trained on real data.
projects.Retro:
Synthetic data was all the rage back in '21/'22. I wanted to use GANs on a more novel usecase than images, so I went with tabular time-series data. We initially experimented with multivariate time-series, but then switched to a univariate series to see if they were even useful in that simplified usecase.

The most difficult thing was figuring out how to evaluate the generated time-series vs original time-series, modifying the models to produce a univariate time-series, and realizing that while synthetic data did help somewhat in downstream ML tasks, the effect was not significant.

This project inspired me to take Probabilistic Time-series Analysis (and all the suffering that came with it)

The best part? This paper was published pre-GPT, so every line is 100% human written.

projects.name: Accelerating Narrative Identification in Conflict Regions with Artificial Intelligence
projects.subtitle: Narrative Detection Assistance tool Using RAGs
projects.description:
Humanitarian analysts working in conflict regions spend hours manually searching audio transcripts for entities and narratives of interest. We built a RAG-based question-answering system over radio broadcast datasets from Africa that retrieves the most relevant transcript segments for a given query and returns a grounded answer with source citations and highlighted audio clips.

The core challenge was retrieval quality at scale — we addressed this with a novel GraphRAG system using a multi-query retriever, which outperformed standard retrieval approaches with a win-rate (win-rate measures how many of the best answers were produced by each model. 'Best' in this case was determined by the accuracy and comprehensiveness of the answer (for instance, citing every entity relevant to the query with its correct name, as determined by human raters) of 58.6% compared to a standard RAG approach, which had a win-rate of 34.5%

images.caption: A screenshot from our application platform illustrating the query answer structure. Note that uniquely, our compound AI system enables us to retrieve the pre and post-answer context such that query responses are presented within an appropriately nuanced discussion on the radio. This is important both for reducing false positives which incur further investigative costs but also reducing false negatives that may be important in the context of surrounding narratives.

projects.name: Benchmarking RAG Methods for Financial Question-Answering
projects.subtitle: Can LLMs Replace Finance Bros?
projects.description:
Financial documents are notoriously difficult for LLMs — they mix structured tables, unstructured text, and specialized terminology, making factual accuracy a real challenge. We benchmarked advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques on the FinanceBench dataset across three query types:

- **Domain-relevant:** questions generically relevant to the financial analysis of companies (such as whether it has paid a dividend in the last year)
- **Metrics-generated:** questions that require numerical reasoning and calculations related to financial metrics (such as the asset turnover ratio of the firm)
- **Novel-generated:** questions added by annotators to be more challenging and involve deeper financial reasoning (such as whether a company's business is subject to cyclicity)

Starting from a baseline accuracy of 37%, we evaluated 6 RAG approaches — including better chunking strategies, reranking, and hybrid retrieval — ultimately reaching 54% accuracy. The results highlight both the promise and the remaining gaps in applying RAG to high-stakes financial QA.

projects.name: Behavior Risk Factor Surveillance Survey (BRFSS) 2013
projects.subtitle: Does Going to Bed at a Reasonable Hour Correlate to Better Health?
projects.description:
I designed several questions using this survey's codebook and description. I then used R, which I was learning at the time, to design visualizations that answered these questions. The questions were:

• Are people diagnosed with COPD(Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) likely to have smoked at least a 100 cigarettes?
• Does the time spent walking and sleeping impact the general health of college age people (18 - 24Y)?
• How does feeling of worthlessness vary among people of different employment status (students, retirees, employed for wages and homemakers) and is this feeling related to annual household income?

projects.name: What are the Most Time-consuming Challenges WIC-eligible Families Face in Securing Food and Resources for their Child?
projects.subtitle: Helping Lulo Understand WIC-eligible Families Better
projects.description:
Design Thinking with Carolyn Hou was the only non-STEM class I took in graduate school. I realized learning to know what to build will become significantly more valuable than knowing how to build, and this class offered a chance to do just that.

Our course project involved helping Lulo, a startup that helps families covered under the Woman, Infant, Child (WIC) assistance program find exactly what grocery items are covered under the program in their local grocery stores through a mobile app.

The ask was to explore how WIC-eligible families could be supported in other ways. To find out, we conducted detailed interviews with 11 individuals across 6 states that met the program's criteria, parsed the transcripts for broader themes, derived insights and then presented our final recommendations to Lulo leadership.

We made note of our own assumptions around what folks might need help with, which revolved around improving access, but what we heard was very different. My favorite insight:

The vast majority of household labor was still shouldered by women, and while they had access to courses and other support resources, the sheer amount of time spent meal prepping, grocery shopping and scouring chat groups, reddit, Facebook groups for coupons and other hacks ("jugaars" in our local lingo) to save money meant they could never meaningfully pursue these opportunities.

**Our recommendations:**
- Add a community-inspired meal planning section, where users can see recipes that can be made entirely using WIC-covered ingredients. This would ease the burden of browsing through several, often conflicting information sources.

- A ratings system
  - Allow users to rate grocery stores in their locality based on:
    - Number of WIC items in stock
    - Healthy (fruits, vegetables, canned beans) foods covered
    - Number of Infant items (formula milk etc) covered

**What I learnt:**
How to talk to people, and more importantly, how to listen.
